notes.title: Search for text inside files
notes.body:
- `grep` searches text for a matching pattern.
- `-r` searches recursively through subfolders.
- `-n` prints matching line numbers.
- Substitute a relevant search term and directory.
- Some log files require elevated permission.
notes.gotcha: Quote search phrases containing spaces. Large searches may return lots of output.

notes.title: SSH into a VirtualBox RHEL lab VM
notes.body: Example for a personal lab VM with NAT port forwarding from host port 2222 to guest port 22. Replace `user` with your lab username.
notes.gotcha: Port 2222 is on the host; SSH inside the guest typically listens on port 22. Use your actual forwarding rule.

notes.title: Exit long command output
notes.body: Some terminal commands display output using the `less` pager. Press `q` to return to the shell prompt. `q` is a keypress, not a command to type at the shell.
notes.gotcha: If the screen appears frozen in a long listing, check whether a pager is open.

notes.title: Show interface addresses
notes.body: Shows a concise summary of network interfaces, their states, and addresses. Useful as a first check when troubleshooting connectivity.
notes.gotcha: The address alone does not prove the interface can reach the destination.

notes.title: Check NetworkManager device status
notes.body: Lists NetworkManager-known devices and their connection states. Use to spot disconnected or unmanaged interfaces.
notes.gotcha: An unmanaged device may be controlled elsewhere, including Open vSwitch.

notes.title: Show selected NetworkManager connection fields
notes.body: Lists saved/active connection profiles with name, UUID, type, and associated device. Compare with `nmcli device status` when a connection is missing.
notes.gotcha: A saved profile is not necessarily active. The DEVICE column may show --.

notes.title: Activate a NetworkManager connection
notes.body: Brings up a specified saved NetworkManager connection profile. Substitute the exact profile name as shown by `nmcli connection show`.
notes.gotcha: This can interrupt connectivity; on remote systems, confirm the correct profile and have an approved recovery path.

notes.title: Set static IPv4 address on a connection profile
notes.body: Changes the IPv4 address stored in the selected NetworkManager profile. This example uses the documentation-only TEST-NET-1 range. You may also need to set `ipv4.method manual` and activate the profile for the change to apply.
notes.gotcha: Modifying a profile is not the same as applying it. Do not copy addresses from operational systems.

notes.title: Set a static IPv4 route via NetworkManager
notes.body: Adds a static route to a connection profile. The first address is the destination network; the second is the next-hop gateway. Both are documentation example addresses.
notes.gotcha: Use +ipv4.routes to append rather than replace existing routes. Check routing before applying.

notes.title: Display IPv4 routing table
notes.body: Shows the kernel IPv4 routing table. Useful to verify the current default route, destination networks, gateways and interfaces.
notes.gotcha: This shows active kernel routes, which may differ from saved connection profiles.

notes.title: Show IPv4 properties for a NetworkManager device
notes.body: Displays general details and IPv4 information of a chosen network interface. Substitute an actual interface name from `nmcli device status`.
notes.gotcha: Use `nmcli device show` for device state; `nmcli connection show` describes saved profiles.

notes.title: Show addresses in compact form
notes.body: Shows interface names, states, and assigned addresses in a compact display. Helpful when comparing multiple devices quickly.
notes.gotcha: An assigned IP address does not establish route or connectivity.

notes.title: List Layer 2 interfaces
notes.body: Shows detailed network link attributes and interface state. Useful when diagnosing virtual interfaces or bridges.
notes.gotcha: Some properties require additional commands or privileges to inspect.

notes.title: Troubleshoot from the real error, not assumptions
notes.body: Reproduce the issue, then open the actual application log. Capture the full exception and the operation that triggered it. A successful SSH connection does not prove a later identity lookup succeeded. Fix the line that raises the exception and verify the full workflow afterward. Example: `must be str or None, not list` can arise when a list is passed into a string API, including `text.split([-1])` instead of `text.split()[-1]`.
notes.gotcha: The same error text can have multiple causes. Trace it to the failing line before editing. Use sanitized logs only.

notes.title: Python: split a label and select its last word
notes.body: `split()` without arguments separates a string on whitespace and returns a list of words. `[-1]` indexes the last item of that list. Writing `split([-1])` passes a list as the separator and raises `TypeError: must be str or None, not list`.
notes.gotcha: Check that the string is nonempty before using `[-1]` if the input can be blank.

notes.title: Python subprocess and SSH: command argument types
notes.command:
args = ['ssh', 'user@192.0.2.10', 'cat /path/to/example.env']
result = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, check=True)
text = result.stdout.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
notes.body: `subprocess.run()` accepts a list of local executable arguments. The SSH destination and remote shell command are each individual string arguments. Read the helper's function signature before replacing a remote command string with a list. Captured stdout is commonly bytes unless text mode is enabled; decode it before passing to a text parser.
notes.gotcha: A Python list is correct for the local subprocess argument vector, but a custom SSH helper may require the remote command itself as one string. Documentation-only address shown.

notes.title: Do not assume a remote computer is at subnet +2
notes.command:
ip -br -4 addr
ip route get 192.0.2.70
ping -c 3 192.0.2.70
notes.body: A subnet such as 192.0.2.0/24 defines an address range, not the active host's last octet. Identify the intended host from approved configuration or inventory, then validate reachability and service availability separately. Ping success, SSH reachability, SSH authentication, and application identity are four different checks.
notes.gotcha: Do not scan broad operational address ranges without authorization. An address may be reassigned; never assume an IP permanently identifies a system.

notes.title: Keep verified output separate from temporary transfer jobs
notes.body: Stage transfer chunks, resume state, logs and manifests in a private temporary job directory. Reassemble and SHA-256-verify the original files, then publish only the verified payload into a human-readable destination folder. Retain recovery state for interrupted jobs; delete temp artifacts only after success. Example naming: `05NOV2026_1452_UNIT_24_transfer/example-test.txt`.
notes.gotcha: Do not delete temporary data before successful verification, and do not delete user data during cleanup. Avoid renaming across filesystems without a safe copy/verify fallback.

notes.title: MANTA non-destructive acceptance-test checklist
notes.body: On approved lab or test systems: (1) verify local node banner and application version; (2) discover multiple sources and connect to each with approved credentials; (3) confirm each source is labeled by its actual node identity; (4) transfer a small text file, then compare hashes; (5) inspect date/time + source folder naming and ensure the file is directly inside; (6) test a folder with nested files and file-size display; (7) test rsync and SCP separately; (8) test permitted bandwidth/compression choices; (9) test cancel/resume using disposable data; (10) check logs and recovery behavior after a deliberate failed test. Record expected/actual and PASS/FAIL for each.
notes.gotcha: Keep test data sanitized and disposable. Avoid production-like disruptions, unapproved configuration changes, or transfers across classification boundaries.

notes.title: Locate relevant Python code and validate a build
notes.command:
grep -nE 'def remote_run|def remember_node' app.py
sed -n '100,140p' app.py
python3 -m py_compile app.py
tar -tzf build.tar.gz
sha256sum build.tar.gz
notes.body: `grep -nE` locates relevant functions with line numbers; `sed -n` prints the nearby section; `py_compile` checks syntax but does not prove runtime correctness; `tar -tzf` lists archive contents without extracting; `sha256sum` produces a checksum for integrity comparison. Keep last known-good build for rollback.
notes.gotcha: Compilation is not a functional test. Compare checksums at the receiving end and follow approved media-scan procedures.

notes.title: VoIP: one-way audio and push-to-talk setup
notes.body:
Symptom: Text communications work and one party hears incoming voice, but the other party cannot hear transmitted voice. Network interfaces can show up while audio still fails.

Actual fix in this case: The receiving party had not selected the correct audio output device in the VoIP application. Set the receiving side's output/playback device correctly and retest.

Push-to-talk (PTT) setup reminder:
1. Click the Talk-to-Tech / Push-to-Talk checkbox or control.
2. When prompted to choose the PTT button, PRESS the physical button or keyboard key you intend to use.
3. Confirm only after the application has registered that button/key; do NOT simply click OK without pressing it.
4. Test the PTT button and audio in both directions.

This PTT setup is an important separate check; it was NOT the root cause of this incident.
notes.gotcha: Always check BOTH ends: sender microphone/input and PTT binding, plus receiver speaker/output-device selection. A live microphone level meter does not prove the remote end has selected the correct playback device.
